action: As the club's notice urges, members should be wary of contact posing as the club or related parties, and change any password they reuse elsewhere.
date_note: Security NEXT (24 November) reports the server overload on 12 November and the finding of the leak on 13 November; the club's own notice date is not given on the page.
exec: Security NEXT reports the Giants' fan club system was attacked from outside and member data, including 807,030 email addresses, was leaked.
plain: The Yomiuri Giants baseball club says its fan club member system was attacked from outside and members' data leaked, including 807,030 email addresses. No misuse has been reported so far.

sources.name: Security NEXT: ファンクラブ会員の個人情報が流出 - 読売巨人

summary: Security NEXT reports that the system managing Yomiuri Giants fan club member information was repeatedly attacked from outside and member personal data leaked. The server became overloaded on 12 November; on 13 November the club found 807,030 email addresses had leaked and reported it to the Personal Information Protection Commission. Further investigation found 16,998 names, 12,831 addresses, 15,434 phone numbers and 274 hashed passwords also leaked. The club reported no misuse so far.
title: Yomiuri Giants fan club system attacked from outside; 807,030 member email addresses leaked, Security NEXT reports

validation.note: Only Security NEXT, relaying the club's notice, was read; the club's own page was not found.
